## Source: amazon-inspector (ff1a325fc41cbb1dd7c949031e75946ce0f5f522bae7f63371dcc2c93589ec5d)
The gem's native-extension build script extconf.rb base64-decodes an embedded Ruby payload, writes it to a random path in the temporary directory, and spawns it in the background before running the normal mkmf build. The decoded payload opens a TCP socket to the hardcoded host 45.138.12.177 on port 8090 and bridges that socket to /bin/sh via IO.popen in a persistent loop, granting the remote host interactive shell access on the installer's machine during `gem install`. The payload destination and shell-exec behavior are hidden inside a base64 literal decoded only at install time, with a bare rescue swallowing errors. The behavior is unrelated to the package's stated purpose (a request throttling library) and runs automatically as part of the gem's native extension build phase.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
